attempts.label: CRCNS:hc-11
attempts.paper_title: Diversity in neural firing dynamics supports both rigid and learned hippocampal sequences
attempts.entry_title: Rigid and plastic hippocampal sequences (Grosmark and Buzsaki 2016)
attempts.summary: The paper's central replay finding held up in this data: the sequence content of ripple events rose from sleep before to sleep after novel maze running, and shuffling the cells whose contribution rose most abolished the increase. Its account of rigid and plastic cells held only in part: plastic cells were more place specific, but did not sharpen their fields during running, and rigid cells did not fire significantly faster offline. The larger replay increase in slow-firing cells did not reproduce, and the one in cells with high ripple recruitment held in part. Every claim could be tested, but the events lack the paper's LFP ripple condition, and the cell groups rest on methods the paper leaves open.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Grosmark and Buzsaki (2016) on CRCNS data set hc-11, which holds the spike times, cell types, position and sleep states of eight CA1 recordings in four rats, each a PRE sleep, a novel maze and a POST sleep. It repeats the place-field, ripple-event, Bayesian replay and per cell contribution analyses, splits cells into rigid and plastic and into low and high firing rate groups, and compares their spatial coding, offline firing and pair-wise coactivity.

Quality is the median Mahalanobis distance of a condition's spikes to the centre of all the cluster's kept spikes, and stability the median distance of one condition's spikes to the other's centre, averaged over both orders; the covariance is that of all the cluster's kept spikes (an assumption, which keeps it defined when a condition has few spikes). A cell needs 10 spikes in a condition (a standard choice).
The PCA features are the first 3 per channel of the shank's channel group in the session .xml (Figure S11 legend, 'the PCA features (used in clustering)').
"Only the first spike of bursts" is read two ways: (a) spikes not preceded by one within 6 ms, (b) only spikes that start a burst; both give the same result.
PRE and POST ripple events are the selected events in the yoked windows Y-a; MAZE is running at 5 cm/s or more.

outcomes.statement: The PRE to POST increase in sequence content is attributable to a small number of plastic cells, judged by removing rigid or plastic cells from the replay analysis.
outcomes.source: Figure 2E legend
outcomes.quote: Effect on sequence content of removal of rigid (black) or plastic (gray) neurons. The PRE to POST increase in sequence content is attributable to only a small number of plastic cells.
outcomes.notes: Removing all plastic units of each session and direction; POST - PRE rZ -0.019 (Y-a, D-a; interval -0.036 to -0.002), the interval reaching zero or below under every reading. Removing the rigid units; 0.124 (interval 0.108 to 0.141), above zero under every reading. With all cells 0.096. With the D-b groups (200 shuffles per template), removing the plastic units leaves the interval above zero in all six readings with the Y-a groups (0.031 to 0.044), in four of six with the Y-b groups and in two of six with the Y-c groups; removing the rigid units leaves it above zero everywhere (0.089 to 0.170), and removing plastic units always lowers the change more. Every reading therefore gives at least the partial pattern and some give no more, so by the rule that the outcome is the one all readings give, partially reproduced. D-a groups under Y-b and Y-c were not run; they could not raise the outcome above partial. Outcome changed after verification round 3 from reproduced.
deviations: Ripple events are the paper's population synchrony events without the condition that each holds the peak of an LFP-detected ripple (Materials and Methods, Ripple Event Detection); the LFP is only in tar.gz archives of 70 GB in all, measured to stream at about 23 MB/s (about 55 minutes), and the detector's channel and threshold are not given.

Assumed that the off-line states (quiet waking and NREM) are the data set's NREM, Drowsy (drowsy wake, low movement) and Intermediate (a sub-type of NREM per the data descriptor) epochs, the lab's own scoring (reading S-a); reading S-b needs the LFP and was not run.

The rigid and plastic groups use readings Y-a (last T of PRE, first T of POST), D-a (each event scored with both direction templates, as the Figure S20 legend 'we independently compared the results of each running direction to its null distribution' suggests) and P-a (one-tailed signed-rank test of per-event PCC against zero, the Figure S19B legend), an assumption; under D-b the group sizes are 108 to 113.
The D-b groups were run with 200 circular shuffles per template in place of 1,000, for run time.

outcomes.statement: Testing each place cell's per-event PCC scores between PRE and POST, 2.2% of cells had significantly higher PRE than POST scores and 21.4% significantly higher POST than PRE scores.
outcomes.source: Figure S19C legend
outcomes.quote: 2.2% of cells showed significantly greater PRE compared to POST PCC scores while 21.4% showed higher POST > PRE
outcomes.notes: Y-a, D-a, two one-tailed rank-sum tests per unit over per-event PCC, 565 units; 5.66% PRE > POST and 14.69% POST > PRE (2.2 +- 0.22 and 21.4 +- 2.14). Over the six Y and D readings 3.72 to 6.37% and 13.45 to 15.93%. POST > PRE is the more common direction under every reading.
deviations: Ripple events are the paper's population synchrony events without the condition that each holds the peak of an LFP-detected ripple (Materials and Methods, Ripple Event Detection); the LFP is only in tar.gz archives of 70 GB in all, measured to stream at about 23 MB/s (about 55 minutes), and the detector's channel and threshold are not given.

Assumed that the off-line states (quiet waking and NREM) are the data set's NREM, Drowsy (drowsy wake, low movement) and Intermediate (a sub-type of NREM per the data descriptor) epochs, the lab's own scoring (reading S-a); reading S-b needs the LFP and was not run.

findings.statement: In Gatsby_08022013 the sessInfo file has spike times up to 32,002.4 s, 1,588.7 s past sessDuration (30,413.6 s), which is also the end of the POST epoch; no other session has spikes past its end. The epochs and the descriptor do not say what the extra recording is.

The state epochs mark only Wake (and in two sessions 2 to 81 s of Drowsy) during the MAZE epoch, so the quiet waking on the maze, in which the paper detects MAZE ripple events, is not given. The descriptor does not say which state is the paper's quiet waking; Drowsy (drowsy wake, low movement) was taken for it.

The data set holds no list of the paper's 491 place cells, of its ripple events, or of its 216 strongly contributing and 105 rigid and 105 plastic cells, so the selections cannot be compared cell by cell. Repeating the place-field method gives 565 place units by running direction (504 with a narrower kernel).

The LFP is only in one tar.gz archive per session (5.1 to 9.0 GB compressed, 70 GB in all), and the spike features in others (0.8 to 2.3 GB). A tar.gz cannot be read in part, so reading one LFP channel means streaming and decompressing the whole archive, measured at about 23 MB/s from the bucket (about 55 minutes for the eight sessions).

Position is sampled every 25.6 ms (39.06 Hz); the paper states 39.69 Hz and the descriptor about 39 Hz. The 2D head position is noisy in some sessions; in Gatsby_08022013 the smoothed head speed is above 13 cm/s in 95% of samples, and under 5 cm/s for 0.1 min of the 38.9 min maze epoch.

The Materials and Methods (Rigid and Plastic Cell Classification) name a one-tailed Wilcoxon rank-sum test over each cell's per-event PCC scores for strongly contributing cells; the Figure S19B legend names a one-tailed signed-rank test. With the signed-rank test 222 to 252 units are strongly contributing; with a rank-sum test of observed against cell-shuffled rZ only 22 to 39.

The per-session archives hold one .clu and one .fet file per shank. The cluster ids of the sessInfo files are shank * 100 + cluster; every pyramidal cell has the same spike count in both. The descriptor does not say which columns of the .fet files are the PCA features; they were taken as the first 3 per channel of the shank's group in the session .xml, the last column being the time in 20 kHz samples.

Questions for the paper's authors. (1) Is the 5 cm Gaussian kernel of the place-field analysis its SD or its width? As an SD 565 place units are found, as a full width at half maximum 504 (paper 491). (2) On the linear mazes, is each ripple event scored with both direction templates, or assigned to one direction first by equation 6? Both give the replay results, but the rigid and plastic groups have 121 units each with both templates and 108 to 113 with one. (3) Which test marks a strongly contributing cell (see the paper_inconsistency finding)? (4) Which part of the longer of PRE and POST is kept when the epochs are yoked? (5) Which LFP channel and threshold detect the sharp wave-ripples? (6) In Figure S5B, is observed |r| compared with single shuffled values or with each event's expected null |r|? Only the first gives PRE above the null. (7) In Figure 4B and C, are cells ranked by firing rate within each session or pooled? Within session the low-rate half's coactivity increase exceeds the high-rate half's (p = 0.019), pooled it does not (p = 0.64). (8) How is quiet waking on the maze identified?

entries.name: crcns-hc-11-grosmark-2016
entries.title: Rigid and plastic hippocampal sequences (Grosmark and Buzsaki 2016)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Grosmark and Buzsaki (2016) on CRCNS data set hc-11, which holds the spike times, cell types, position and sleep states of eight CA1 recordings in four rats, each a PRE sleep, a novel maze and a POST sleep. It repeats the place-field, ripple-event, Bayesian replay and per cell contribution analyses, splits cells into rigid and plastic and into low and high firing rate groups, and compares their spatial coding, offline firing and pair-wise coactivity.
